long_biography.plain_text:
Winning a government tender to publish Israel’s telephone directories transformed Morris Kahn’s fortunes after several early ventures failed. He came from a poor South African family and moved to Israel, where bicycle, cattle and glove businesses failed before the directory contract created a durable commercial platform.

Kahn directed much of his wealth to ambitious public projects. He became the driving financial force behind SpaceIL’s privately funded lunar mission, while his philanthropy established a University of Haifa marine research station on the Mediterranean. When the first Beresheet probe crashed on the Moon, he called it a hard landing and emphasised the mission’s educational value.
